drug_class: Biologic / TNF blocker (tumor necrosis factor inhibitor)
purpose: Adalimumab-adaz is used to treat several conditions where the immune system attacks the body, such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and ankylosing spondylitis. It helps reduce pain, swelling, and inflammation. It can also slow down joint damage in certain types of arthritis.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called TNF (tumor necrosis factor) that can cause too much inflammation and damage healthy tissues when there is too much of it. Adalimumab-adaz is a biologic medicine — made from living cells — that attaches to TNF and blocks it from causing that harmful inflammation. Think of it like a sponge that soaks up the troublemaking protein so your body can calm down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include redness, itching, or pain at the injection site, headache, rash, and upper respiratory infections like a stuffy or runny nose. Some people may also experience nausea or stomach pain.
warnings: This medication lowers your immune system's ability to fight infections, so you are more likely to get serious infections, including tuberculosis (TB). Your doctor will test you for TB before you start. Tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, cough, or feel very unwell. There is also a small increased risk of certain cancers. Do not get live vaccines while taking this medicine. Let all your healthcare providers know you are on this medication.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually every other week for most adult conditions, though the dose and schedule can vary depending on your specific condition. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to inject it at home. It comes in a prefilled pen or syringe to make it easier to use.
